payload.summary: All five amendments identify real, verified mass conservation defects in the tank simulation. CleanFilter and SiphonDetritus silently destroy N/C by reducing pools without routing removed mass. Shrimp reproduction creates mass from nothing. Conservation tests only cover the zero-DIC-rate case, missing the preset configuration. The budget tracking system lacks runtime conservation guards in release builds. Each amendment is well-evidenced and proposes a sound remediation path.

votes.rationale: Verified: CleanFilter reduces decomposer/nitrifier biomass by intensity*0.5 but the removed mass vanishes. The shrimp mortality code at shrimp.rs:483-491 demonstrates the correct pattern (routing dead biomass to fine_detritus via live_biomass_detrital_mass_g). CleanFilter should either route removed microbe biomass to detritus or record it as an explicit export in the budget ledger. This is a genuine N/C conservation violation.

Verified: ProcessParams::default() sets both DIC rates to 0.0, while default.toml sets respiration=0.08 and photosynthesis=0.12. The conservation tests use TankState::new() which gets the zero defaults, so they never exercise the DIC flux path that would break carbon conservation. Adding a comment or dedicated test acknowledging this is a low-cost, high-clarity improvement that prevents false confidence in conservation guarantees under realistic parameters.

Verified: SiphonDetritus multiplies particulate_organics_g_total and fine_detritus_g_total by (1-fraction) and returns None (no BudgetDelta). The removed mass is a physical export (siphoning waste out of the tank) that should be recorded. Either route to a BudgetDelta export classification or track as an explicit outflow. This is the same class of conservation violation as CleanFilter.

Verified: At shrimp.rs:371-374, total_successful * 25 juveniles are added to juveniles_count with no mass debit. EggCohort tracks only count and progress_days—no biomass field exists. The existing hatch test only checks population counts, not mass. The existing budget test at budget_tracking.rs:404 explicitly sets hatch_success_base=0.0 to avoid this path. This is a clear mass creation violation that needs an egg biomass pool or explicit source debit, plus a regression test.

Verified: budget.rs:141 uses debug_assert! which compiles out in release. engine.rs:164-168 records and stores ticks but performs no conservation validation. The invariants.rs enforce_invariants function checks non-negativity and range clamping but not conservation laws. A tick-level conservation check (even test-only) would catch issues like the shrimp hatch mass creation immediately rather than relying on ad hoc test coverage. This is a sound defensive measure for a simulation where conservation is a core invariant.
